purpose: Teach: はずす/淋しい/逢い/ぐったり/たいがい/楽々/あわせる/あたえ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは老眼鏡をはずす度に微笑まれたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran — when your father was younger, he'd smile every time he took off his reading glasses.
lines.style: Soft, remembering gaze. Slow, measured pace. Warm and distant at once. Trailing off slightly, as if seeing something only he can see.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お孫様が来られないと淋しいって仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — your grandfather used to say how lonely it was when the grandchildren couldn't come visit.
lines.style: Warm affirmation with gentle nostalgia. Conversational, as if sharing a remembered secret with him. Slight uplift on 'dear' — drawing him back to the present moment with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと毎週逢いに行ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father and I went to see his father every single week.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact underneath the gentleness. Steady, unadorned rhythm. Small emphasis on 'every week' — the quiet pride of consistency. Eyes held forward, not seeking agreement.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、暑い日にぐったりしてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather used to get so worn out on hot days, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle observation phrased as shared memory. Knowing tone — she's checking with him. Soft, caring. The 'dear' sits at the end like a hand being placed on his arm.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「たいがいの事は時間が解決する」と仰ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, your father used to say: 'Most things are solved by time.'
lines.style: Reflective pause before the quote. Lower register on the saying itself — as if quoting him directly, preserving his voice. Lingering slightly on the words, letting them settle.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、難しい仕事も楽々こなされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He took on difficult work so gracefully, though, didn't he? Your grandfather was like that.
lines.style: Warm acknowledgment. Quiet pride underneath. Conversational but measured — not overstating, just recognizing what she knows to be true. The 'didn't he' is gentle, not challenging.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは家族の時間にあわせる方だったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father always made time for family. He adjusted his whole life around it.
lines.style: Steady voice, deliberate in its sincerity. No flourish — just stating a fact that moved him. Slight emphasis on 'adjusted' — understanding what that cost him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様にお小遣いをあたえて下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he was so generous with the grandchildren, wasn't he? Always giving them pocket money, your grandfather.
lines.style: Warm, intimate recollection. The 'wasn't he' is rhetorical, almost conspiratorial — she's not asking, she's reminding him he already knows. Closes on a soft note, like a lullaby.
